ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2016; Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018; Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2010; International Companies Regulations and related directives of the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL).

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders, UBOs, and controlling persons must be screened at onboarding and on a continuing basis against the UN Consolidated List, Samoa consolidated sanctions list maintained by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (Samoa FIU), OFAC SDN List, and FATF public statements. PEPs are treated as higher risk, requiring enhanced due diligence and senior management approval. Screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years by the licensed registered agent under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – available via counter, email lodgment, and SIRIS e-filing channel for name reservation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the working language of the register. Company names must be expressed in Roman characters. Foreign-language names require a certified Romanized transliteration. Names in the Samoan language that imply a connection with the Government, public bodies, or misleading local significance are rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal to the Registrar within 14 days of the rejection notice, providing legal argument and a revised name if required. If the Registrar maintains the rejection, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa within 30 days. A fresh reservation with alternative acceptable name choices may be resubmitted immediately without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible as the statutory registered office. The International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa at the premises of its licensed registered agent. The studio's operational and back-office functions may be conducted remotely from outside Samoa.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – estimated <10% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first fiscal year for a low-risk, non-licensed digital services company. The Registrar and the Samoa FIU retain inspection powers under the International Companies Act 1987 and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended; particularly ss. 6 (incorporation), 8 (name), 10 (registered office), 13 (share capital) and 21-26 (directors and secretary); tax exemption confirmed under the International Business Activities Act 1998.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Companies and Trusts Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 Application for Incorporation of an International Company together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required; capital may be expressed in any currency; no escrow deposit or capitalisation account is mandated by the International Companies Act 1987.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF WS INTERNATIONAL COMPANY (in formation): RESOLVED THAT: (1) The initial subscriber subscribes for one ordinary share of US$1.00, such share is allotted at par, and the share register is opened. (2) The registered office is fixed at the office of the authorised registered agent in Apia, Samoa, and such agent is approved as agent. (3) The first director and the first secretary are appointed on the terms recorded in the board minutes. (4) The officers are authorised to file the incorporation instrument and to do all acts required to obtain banking facilities and tax-exemption status. (5) The chairperson is authorised to certify this resolution. This resolution takes effect on incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request stating the proposed company name and confirming that no restricted or prohibited words are used. The Registrar examines the proposed name against the reserved names database and issues a name clearance certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or prohibited character, submit alternative names or a written consent from the existing name holder; re-submission within 14 days is accepted without an additional government filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and execution of constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent in Samoa and notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English in full compliance with the International Companies Act 1987. The subscriber executes the documents before a notary or witness, and the registered agent signs the consent to act as registered agent and provide the Apia registered office.
required_dossiers: Registered agent's consent and registered office address
Power of attorney if execution is made by delegate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where notarial certification is defective, the signature page is re-executed with a corrected notarial block and the original notarised copy is retained for filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL (online filing portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the application for incorporation by submitting Form 1 together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association and the registered agent's consent. The statutory filing fee is paid electronically at the time of submission.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a Registrar's requisition within 14 days by amending the relevant schedule or supplying missing evidence. If the application is formally refused, a fresh application must be lodged with corrected documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate issuance and government fee settlement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Companies Registry, MCIL cashier and online payment gateway
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After assessment, the prescribed government filing fee of US$150 is confirmed and settled. The Registrar verifies payment and issues the Certificate of Incorporation together with stamped constitutional documents.
required_dossiers: Government fee invoice or payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not issued within the service standard, escalate to the Registry's client services unit. Minor data entry errors are corrected through a formal rectification request and reprint of the certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First board of directors and licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, adopt the First Board Resolution, open the statutory registers, issue the share certificate, appoint the registered agent and corporate officers, adopt the common seal, and obtain the Certificate of Good Standing for bank account opening.
required_dossiers: Director and secretary consents to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Administrative omissions in minutes or share certificates are cured by a supplemental board resolution and the reissue of corrected statutory records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Business and Industry Development Division; Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating licence is required for AI subtitle transcription and voice-cloning studio services; general Building Occupancy Permit and Fire Safety Certificate remain mandatory for physical premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) - Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Permitted office-based activity; no full EIA report required. Development consent is required only for physical fit-out or structural alterations exceeding PUMA minor works thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No manufacturing wastewater or VOC-emitting processes are present. Compliance with Samoa clean air standards, trade waste discharge limits, and authorised e-waste disposal through MNRE-endorsed recyclers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA); structural load and electrical installation clearance under the Samoa National Building Code; workplace health and safety audit under the Samoa Occupational Safety and Health regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), Government of Samoa; official portal and e-services gateway: https://www.sra.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate the International Company (IC) with the Samoa International Companies Registry, appointing a licensed registered agent and registered office in Samoa. 2. Obtain the Certificate of Incorporation; the IC is automatically a non-resident exempt person under the International Companies Act 1987. 3. Apply to the Samoa Revenue Authority for a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) only if a Samoa tax presence is created; submission requires the prescribed TIN application form, certificate of incorporation, registered-agent confirmation, and beneficial-owner identification. 4. Register for VAGST separately if the IC makes taxable supplies in Samoa or exceeds the WST 100,000 turnover threshold. 5. For a fully offshore AI post-production subtitle and dubbing operation with no Samoa taxable activity, no TIN/VAT registration or tax return filing is required, but appropriate non-resident client and foreign-consumption evidence must be maintained.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election and no hybrid mismatch election exist in Samoa. An International Company automatically receives exempt status and may elect to convert to a domestic Samoa company, which would subject it to ordinary Samoa income tax and VAGST on Samoa-source activity. A non-residence certificate may be obtained from the Samoa Ministry for Revenue to evidence tax-exempt status for foreign counterparties.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time electronic invoicing clearance or digital stamping regime is currently imposed by Samoa. Businesses may issue paper or electronic VAGST tax invoices; the SRA does not require API-based fiscal clearance. Standard invoice content must show the supplier's name, TIN, recipient details, description, date, VAGST-exclusive amount, VAGST amount, and total. Electronic records must be retained and accessible for audit in Samoa.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Samoa's VAGST Act 2008, zero-rating applies to goods physically exported from Samoa and to services supplied to a non-resident recipient where the benefit and use of the services occur outside Samoa. For the AI subtitle transcription and voice cloning studio, the following conditions must be met: the contract is with an overseas studio, platform, or rights holder; the deliverables are digitally transmitted outside Samoa; payment is received from outside Samoa; and no Samoan audience or local market exploitation is made available. Services auxiliary to exported goods may also be zero-rated if the direct benefit is linked to the exported goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (for physical goods; for pure digital services, a Declaration of Export of Services is used)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (for physical media; not required for pure digital delivery)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/credit advice proving foreign exchange receipt from abroad
Signed service contract with the non-resident client
Digital delivery log, download/use record, and technical service report demonstrating offshore consumption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Samoa Revenue Authority may audit export zero-rating claims. If export or foreign-consumption evidence is deficient, the SRA will reverse the zero rating and assess VAGST at 15% on the supply value, with statutory interest. Civil penalties vary by culpability: a shortfall penalty for failure to take reasonable care, and a higher penalty for intentional evasion or fraud. Fraudulent export documentation may also trigger criminal prosecution, fines, and imprisonment. Retrospective clawbacks are governed by the Tax Administration Act 2012, with extended periods for fraudulent claims.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Annual Government License Fee (International Company; fee tiered by authorized capital, standard tier assumes nominal capital not exceeding USD 10,000)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Government of Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary of incorporation; Annual Return must be delivered within 30 days after each incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% of the outstanding annual fee; continued default triggers the Registrar's gazetted notice of intention to strike off and eventual administrative strike-off from the International Companies Register, resulting in loss of corporate capacity and vesting of assets in the Crown; reinstatement requires a Court restoration order and settlement of all arrears and penalties

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit for International Companies; an audit arises only where the company's constitution requires it or members pass a resolution requesting audited financial statements
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No designated statutory accounting framework for exempt International Companies; where audited financial statements are prepared, IFRS as issued by the IASB or Samoa-adopted accounting standards are accepted

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Register of Beneficial Owners is confidential and maintained exclusively by the licensed registered agent in Samoa; no annual UBO filing is submitted to the Ministry. The agent must re-identify and re-verify beneficial owners at least annually under AML/CFT obligations and must update the Register of Members and the UBO Register whenever share transfers are lodged, preserving the complete prior ownership chain as a permanent record

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 750 - USD 1,500 per annum for a licensed registered agent in Samoa
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 4,000 per annum where an audit is voluntarily elected or member-required; otherwise USD 0

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective rate for a qualifying Samoa International Company (IC) licensed under the International Companies Act 2007. The IC is exempt from income tax, capital gains tax, dividend withholding tax, interest/royalty withholding tax and stamp duty on all non-Samoan-source income provided it does not carry on business in Samoa. Ordinary Samoa-resident companies are taxed at 27% with no general tax holiday regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: SRA Form IR-1 (Annual Income Tax Return) filed through the Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA) e-Services / Taxpayer Access Portal. Exempt International Companies do not file IR-1; they file an Annual Declaration with the Registrar of International Companies through the licensed Samoan registered agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Taxable companies must also make quarterly provisional tax instalments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual IR-1 return is due by the gazetted statutory date, ordinarily within three months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., by 31 March for a 31 December year-end). Quarterly provisional instalments are due within one month of each quarter. Exempt ICs pay the annual government licence fee on the anniversary of incorporation and file the Annual Declaration on or before that anniversary date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, Tax Identification Number (TIN) and registered office in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State that the company is a non-resident IC and insert the appointed Samoan licensed agent's code and address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross assessable income derived from sources in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter nil unless the IC is impermissibly carrying on business in Samoa; attach a certification of non-residence and offshore income only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions and expenses attributable to assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Leave blank where the IC exemption applies; do not claim overheads or intercompany charges as deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory taxable income (assessable income less allowable deductions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter nil and cross-reference the exemption under the International Companies Act 2007.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable at 27% before credits and provisional tax payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter nil. If tax has been computed, claim the IC statutory exemption and any applicable foreign tax credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification signed by two directors or a director and the company secretary, or by the licensed agent on behalf of a non-resident IC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The licensed Samoan agent countersigns and files the Annual Declaration with the Registrar of International Companies in lieu of an income tax return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of an IR-1 return attracts a late filing penalty plus late payment interest on the unpaid tax; deliberate default is subject to evasion penalties of up to three times the tax shortfall and imprisonment. An IC failing to file the Annual Declaration or pay the annual licence fee incurs a late payment surcharge and risks strike-off from the International Companies Register, with restoration only by court order or Registrar's discretion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on dividends paid by an ordinary Samoa-resident company to shareholders. Distributions by a qualifying tax-exempt International Company to non-resident shareholders are statutorily exempt from Samoan dividend withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident claiming DTA relief under Samoa's limited treaty network (principally the Samoa–New Zealand comprehensive double tax agreement) must deliver to the Samoa Revenue Authority: (i) a completed DTA withholding declaration form, (ii) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the jurisdiction of residence, and (iii) proof of beneficial ownership, before or at the point of remittance. The reduced rate is applied via prior written approval or refund claim. For exempt ICs, domestic law already provides exemption, so no treaty claim is required.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory final withholding is 15% on cross-border interest and 15% on royalties paid by taxable Samoan payers; a lower treaty rate (generally 10-15%) applies if the beneficial owner supplies a valid TRC. Royalties and interest paid by an exempt IC are outside the Samoan withholding net because the IC derives no Samoan-source income.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa has no gazetted statutory Local File / Master File monetary threshold; the SRA may apply the arm's length principle and the general anti-avoidance rule to related-party transactions under the Income Tax Act 1974 and Tax Administration Act 2012. Prudent compliance practice: prepare and retain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local File style) where annual connected-party turnover in the AI subtitle and dubbing value chain exceeds WST 1,000,000 or where large IP royalty or licence payments are made to other group entities.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies Act 2007 and the related Economic Substance Rules require Samoan licensed ICs to demonstrate substantial local economic presence when conducting relevant activities (including financing, leasing, distribution and service centres, IP holding, trust and fiduciary services). The IC must maintain a registered office and licensed agent in Samoa, keep adequate accounting records locally, and have proportionate physical premises, resident employees, local board meetings and expenditure. A passive shell used merely as a tax conduit will be denied the tax exemption and reclassified as taxable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Income and Withholding Tax Declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful suppression of Samoan-source revenue, issuing false invoices for AI subtitle or dubbing services, or claiming the IC tax exemption while secretly conducting business in and deriving income from Samoa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty tax up to 200% of the tax shortfall plus late payment interest; criminal fines and imprisonment up to 7 years; any tax advantage and exemption is disgorged retroactively.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who caused or knowingly aided the evasion are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax; travel bans and imprisonment apply on conviction; the corporate veil is pierced where the IC is a mere facade.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Samoa IC with no physical office, no resident staff, no local decision-making and no real activity, with transactions routed solely to avoid tax in counterparty jurisdictions or through the AI licensing chain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of the IC's tax-exempt status, re-assessment at the 27% corporate rate, denial of treaty benefits, penalties up to WST 100,000 for false substance declarations, and deregistration from the International Companies Register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil recovery from personal assets, disqualification from acting as directors of any Samoan licensed entity, and blocking notices restricting international travel where the Registrar determines reckless or fraudulent use of the IC.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Beneficial Ownership and Counterparty Due Diligence Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify and file current beneficial ownership information, use of undisclosed nominee directors, accepting Stripe/Wise payments without adequate AML/KYC verification, or failing to report suspicious transactions to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act, companies face monetary penalties and the licensed agent may be fined or deregistered; non-compliant ICs are liable to submission of transaction monitoring reports and confiscation of funds linked to money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable for systemic AML failures, with imprisonment, travel bans and permanent debarment from management of regulated Samoan entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting AI dubbing, subtitling licence or post-production intercompany payments at non-arm's length prices, generating excessive deductible royalties, or accumulating economic profits in Samoa without corresponding local value creation and substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SRA re-characterisation of the transaction, disallowance of excessive deductions, shortfall penalties of up to 50%, imposition of interest on the corrected liability, and cancellation of treaty or exemption benefits where the recipient is not the true beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the related-party agreements may be assessed personally for the corrected tax shortfall and, where the conduct is deliberate, prosecuted for tax default with imprisonment and travel restrictions.
